extracted.intended_audience: fiction writers and memoirists (aspiring and practicing)
extracted.subtask_description: Advice on the craft of storytelling focused on how to choose, shape, and present events and characters in short fiction and memoir. Emphasizes selection, perspective, and the imposition of form to make experience meaningful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stories as self-definition
rubrics_metrics.description: We come to know ourselves and even define ourselves by the stories that we tell about ourselves that we decide is our story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the selection of which story you tell as an act of self-definition; recognize storytelling as a lifelong process in which the narrator (or writer) chooses which events constitute 'the story' and thereby shapes identity and meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and omission (editing experience)
rubrics_metrics.description: The very process of making a story means carving out and leaving out all kinds of things, editing our experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be economical and deliberate: decide what to exclude as well as what to include. Example given: a child telling about a teacher's unfairness is leaving out many facts — the omissions are part of how the story functions. Good storytelling requires ruthless editing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impose pattern/form on experience
rubrics_metrics.description: We can’t make all of [experience] mean anything, so we have to find or impose some pattern on it to make sense of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A story must give experience shape — seek or create patterns, structure, and form that make disparate events cohere and convey meaning. Structure is not optional; it is how experience becomes intelligible as narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: A story gives only a partial sense of reality
rubrics_metrics.description: So a story always gives us a partial sense of reality, but the only way we can have any sense of reality is to give our experience form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept and work with narrative partiality: truth in fiction/memoir is constructed through selective representation rather than exhaustive factual completeness. Use form to convey a convincing 'partial' reality rather than attempting totality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perspective and differing viewpoints
rubrics_metrics.description: Different people within the story see it in very different ways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay attention to point of view — characters will perceive the same events differently. Use contrasting perspectives to enrich complexity, reveal bias, and create dramatic tension; ensure consistency and clarity in whose viewpoint is being presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inhabiting the minds of others (character interiority/empathy)
rubrics_metrics.description: The never-ending mysteries and revelations that come from spending one’s time inhabiting the minds of others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate the ability to enter and render characters' interior lives empathetically and accurately. Deep character interiority is a craft habit — spend time imagining and dramatizing others' thoughts, motives, and perceptions to generate insight and realism.
